name: s1-constant-sweep-v1
purpose: Produce a real results.tsv on real train.py / real GPU (review S1). Deterministic proposer stands in for the LLM so the numeric half of S1 lands without agent plumbing.
notes: Descriptions are written in agent-card voice on purpose, but they are AUTHORED, not LLM-generated. Silhouette measured on this data bounds card diversity from above; it does not replace real LLM cards (review C1/S1).

DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and EVAL_BATCH_SIZE are deliberately absent: on a supported consumer GPU the fork's autotune picks the train batch from gpu_profile.train_batch_candidates (train.py:857) and the eval batch from gpu_profile.eval_batch_cap (train.py:1298), so editing those module constants is a silent no-op.

category is the GROUND-TRUTH label. scas.replay re-derives a label by keyword; analyze.py reports the disagreement, which is the first real measurement of the router's error rate (review C1 cites ~43% on one class from fixtures).
Every value for a given constant is distinct across the plan, so a kept edit can never make a later edit a no-op.
The loop is keep-or-revert against the running best, exactly as program.md prescribes, so later experiments compose on top of earlier wins.

experiments.description: first run after clone, no changes, establishing the baseline val_bpb for this GPU
raise the Muon matrix learning rate from 0.04 to 0.06, the loss curve looked under-driven early so more step size should buy faster progress inside the budget
go deeper, 8 to 10 transformer layers, trading steps for capacity now that the budget is fixed
back the decay penalty right off to 0.05, at this token count the model is almost certainly underfitting rather than overfitting
add a short warmup over the first 2 percent of the schedule to stop the early updates from thrashing the embeddings
drop the banded sliding-window layers and give every block full causal attention over the whole context
push the embedding learning rate to 0.9, token embeddings converge slowly and they are cheap to move
double the decay penalty instead, testing the opposite hypothesis that shrinking weights keeps the matrices better conditioned for Muon
widen the residual stream, aspect ratio 64 to 96, favouring width over depth at constant layer count
smooth the AdamW first moment, beta1 0.8 to 0.9, gradients on this data look noisy step to step
spend less of the run decaying, cut the cooldown fraction to 0.3 so the model holds a high learning rate for longer
halve the attention head dimension to 64, doubling head count at the same model width for finer-grained mixing
remove the decay term entirely as a clean control, if it is worthless the simpler code wins on the simplicity criterion
let the output head move faster, unembedding lr 0.004 to 0.006, since bits per byte is dominated by the final projection
go shallower instead, 6 layers, buying a lot more optimizer steps inside the same five minutes
halve the tokens per optimizer step to 256K, doubling the number of updates the schedule gets to make
settle the decay question with a middling penalty of 0.3 between the two extremes already tried
lengthen the banded pattern so only every fifth block sees full context, cheaper attention should buy more steps
stop annealing all the way to zero, hold a floor at 10 percent of peak so the last stretch still learns something
halve the scalar and gate learning rate to 0.25, those parameters are few and were probably overshooting
try the narrow direction, aspect ratio down to 48, a thinner residual stream at the same depth
one more decay setting at 0.1 to map the curve properly rather than guessing between two sampled points
lengthen the AdamW second moment window, beta2 0.95 to 0.99, for a steadier per-parameter step size
push depth to 12 layers and find out where the capacity-versus-steps trade actually turns over
the other direction on batch, 1M tokens per step, fewer but much less noisy updates
extend warmup to 5 percent of the run in case the short version was still too abrupt for the deeper model
